questions.q: What type of stress occurs when two forces act on a body in opposite directions, tending to pull it apart or elongate it?
questions.n: Tension is the internal stress that results from applied loads tending to elongate or pull a structural element apart.

questions.q: Which internal force is characterized by a "squashing" action, where external loads tend to shorten or crush a structural member?
questions.n: Compression is the stress state where the material is pushed together, leading to shortening or crushing of the member.

questions.q: What do you call the structural stress caused by forces acting perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of a member, often seen in beams?
questions.n: Shear stress occurs when forces act perpendicular to the member's axis, tending to cause parts of it to slide against each other.

questions.q: In structural engineering, what is "Axial Load"?
o: A load that acts perpendicular to the longitudinal axis
A load that is applied at an angle to the axis
A load that acts directly along the longitudinal axis of a structural member, passing through its center of gravity.
A load that causes a member to twist
questions.n: Axial loads act in line with the member's axis, creating either pure tension or pure compression.

questions.q: What is the term for the maximum load that a system, or a specific soil type, can support without undergoing failure or excessive settlement?
questions.n: Bearing capacity is the measure of the soil's ability to resist the pressure applied by a foundation without failing structurally or settling too much.

questions.q: Why is "Concrete Cover" critical for reinforcing bars in structural members?
o: To make the concrete look smoother
To protect the steel from corrosion (oxidation) and to provide fire resistance.
To increase the weight of the beam
questions.n: The alkaline nature of concrete protects steel from rust, and the thickness acts as an insulator against heat during a fire.

questions.q: What is the standard concrete cover for footings cast against and permanently exposed to earth?
questions.n: The NSCP and ACI codes require 75mm (3 inches) for concrete cast against the ground due to high moisture and soil contact.

questions.q: What is the function of a "Sag Rod" in a steel roof framing system?
o: To act as the main drainage pipe
To provide lateral support for purlins and prevent them from sagging or twisting under the weight of the roofing.
To connect the truss to the column
questions.n: Sag rods help maintain the alignment of purlins, especially on steep roofs, preventing them from bowing or rotating.

questions.q: In a composite slab section, what is the primary purpose of a "Shear Stud" welded to the steel beam?
o: To act as a spacer for the floor tiles
To transfer horizontal shear between the concrete slab and the steel beam, ensuring they act together as a single structural unit.
To prevent the beam from rusting
To provide a hanging point for utilities
questions.n: Shear studs prevent slippage between the concrete and steel, creating a 'composite' member that is stronger and stiffer.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of top bars (reinforcement) in a continuous concrete slab?
o: To make the slab easier to walk on during construction
To resist negative bending moments that occur over the structural supports (beams or walls).
To resist positive bending moments at the center of the span
questions.n: In continuous spans, the slab tends to bend upward over the supports, creating tension at the top that the top bars must resist.

questions.q: In a Fire Detection and Alarm System (FDAS) diagram, what does the "Initiating Device Circuit" (IDC) typically connect?
o: The backup batteries to the main power
The fire alarm panel to the building's public address system
The smoke detectors to the sprinkler heads
It connects manual pull stations and smoke/heat detectors to the fire alarm control panel.
questions.n: The IDC 'initiates' the alarm signal when a sensor or manual station is triggered.

questions.q: When analyzing a building's FDAS layout, what is the standard maximum floor area that a single smoke detector can typically cover?
o: Approximately 60 to 90 square meters (depending on ceiling height and local fire codes).
The entire floor of a standard house
questions.n: Based on NFPA and standard practices, smoke detectors are generally rated for a 9m x 9m area in ideal conditions.

questions.q: In an FDAS wiring diagram, why is the gauge or size of the wire (e.g., TFPN vs. THHN) critical for the system's integrity?
o: Because thicker wires are easier to bend
To make sure the wire fits inside the conduit
To ensure minimal voltage drop and to maintain fire-rated performance during an emergency.
To match the color of the walls
questions.n: Wires must be thick enough to carry the signal without loss and must withstand heat to function when a fire occurs.

questions.q: What is the term for the number of times the total air volume of a room is completely replaced with fresh or recirculated air in one hour?
questions.n: ACH (Air Changes per Hour) is the standard metric for ventilation efficiency and hygiene.

questions.q: What is the typical recommended Air Change Rate (ACH) for a standard office space?
o: 4 to 10 air changes per hour (depending on occupancy and equipment).
None, offices use natural ventilation only
questions.n: This range provides adequate ventilation for office activities and equipment heat dissipation.

questions.q: For a high-traffic area like a restaurant dining room, is the required Air Change Rate higher or lower than a standard storage room?
o: Higher (typically 8 to 12 ACH or more to manage odors and CO2 levels).
It depends only on the number of windows
questions.n: Dense occupancy and food odors necessitate more frequent air replacement to maintain air quality.

questions.q: Which type of plumbing pipe is most commonly used for "Main Cold Water Lines" in Philippine high-rise construction?
o: PPR (Polypropylene Random Copolymer) or Galvanized Iron (GI) for older high-spec systems.
questions.n: PPR is current standard for its durability and heat-fusion joints; GI was common in older heritage or high-spec projects.

questions.q: For sanitary and vent lines (waste management), which brand/material is considered a standard for high-quality exterior and interior drainage in the Philippines?
o: PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride) Series 1000 (often Neltex, Moldex, or Atlanta).
questions.n: Series 1000 is the thicker, high-quality standard for sanitary systems in the Philippines.

questions.q: What is the most recommended material for exterior wall cladding in areas with high seismic activity and moisture exposure?
o: Fiber Cement Board (e.g., HardieFlex) or Light Gauge Steel Framing with specialized exterior finishes.
questions.n: These materials are lightweight (good for seismic loads) and resistant to rotting, warping, and moisture.

questions.q: When installing bricks or CHB in a wall, what is the term for the pattern where units are shifted so the vertical joints do not align?
questions.n: Shifting the joints prevents cracks from traveling straight down the wall and increases lateral strength.

questions.q: In a masonry wall, what is the purpose of the "Header" position (placing the brick with its short end facing out)?
o: To save money by using fewer bricks
To create a smooth surface for painting
To tie two wythes (layers) of a brick wall together for structural stability.
questions.n: The header spans across the thickness of the wall, locking the front layer and back layer together.

questions.q: What type of reinforcement is used in a "Footing" to resist the upward pressure of the soil?
o: Bottom reinforcement (tension bars) arranged in a grid.
questions.n: Because the soil pushes up against the footing, the bottom fibers are stretched (in tension).

questions.q: What is the primary structural reason for using a "Mat Foundation" or "Raft Foundation"?
o: To save on the cost of concrete
To distribute heavy loads over a large area when the soil bearing capacity is low or the building loads are very high.
To provide a basement for parking
questions.n: A mat foundation behaves like a giant raft, floating the building over weak soil by using the entire footprint of the structure.

questions.q: Why is it difficult to choose the "best" answer in board exam questions regarding site application?
o: Because the board exam is based on luck
Because all the answers are wrong
Because architects don't need to know site application
Because choices are often "distractors" that are technically correct but not the most "ideal" or "standard" practice under specific code conditions.
questions.n: Licensure exams test judgment by providing several plausible answers where only one fits the specific 'standard' or 'code' requirement best.

questions.q: When analyzing a diagram of a composite slab, what component serves as the permanent formwork for the concrete?
o: The Metal Decking (or Corrugated Steel Deck).
questions.n: In composite systems, the steel deck stays in place, supporting wet concrete and later acting as tension reinforcement.

questions.q: In structural analysis, what do you call the internal moment that causes a beam to bend such that it is concave upward (creating "tension" at the bottom)?
questions.n: Positive moment causes 'sagging,' which results in a concave-up shape and tension at the bottom of the beam.

questions.q: What is the term for a structural member that is subjected primarily to axial compression?
questions.n: Columns are vertical members that carry the weight of the structure above through axial compression.

questions.q: Which structural phenomenon occurs when a thin, slender column fails suddenly under a compression load before the material reaches its ultimate strength?
questions.n: Buckling is a form of instability where a long, slender member bends sideways due to axial compression.

questions.q: What is the "Neutral Axis" of a beam undergoing bending?
o: The layer or line in a beam where there is zero stress (neither tension nor compression).
The bottom edge of the beam
The top edge of the beam
questions.n: It is the theoretical transition zone between the tension and compression zones of the beam.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of "Web Reinforcement" (Stirrups) in a reinforced concrete beam?
o: To prevent the beam from rusting
To increase the compressive strength of concrete
To hold the top and bottom bars in place during pouring
To resist diagonal tension or shear stresses.
questions.n: Concrete is weak in tension; stirrups cross the 45-degree cracks that form due to shear forces.

questions.q: In a cantilever beam, where is the maximum tension reinforcement (top bars) located?
o: At the bottom of the beam, near the support
At the top of the beam, near the support.
In the exact center of the beam's depth
At the free end of the beam
questions.n: A cantilever 'hogs' downward, creating tension at the top surface, which is highest at the fixed support.

questions.q: What does "Modulus of Elasticity" measure in a building material?
o: The melting point of the material
The stiffness of the material or its resistance to elastic deformation.
questions.n: A higher modulus means the material is stiffer and will deform less under the same load.

questions.q: What type of load is a heavy piece of permanent equipment, such as an AHU or a large generator, classified as?
questions.n: Dead loads are permanent components of the building, including its structure and fixed equipment.

questions.q: What is "Deflection" in a structural sense?
o: The degree to which a structural element is displaced under a load.
questions.n: It refers to the vertical or horizontal distance a member moves from its original position when loaded.

questions.q: In seismic analysis, what is the term for the total design lateral force or shear at the base of a structure?
questions.n: Base shear is the estimate of the maximum expected lateral force that will occur due to seismic ground motion at the base of the building.

questions.q: In a Fire Detection and Alarm System, what is a "Zoning" plan?
o: Dividing the building into manageable areas so that the source of a fire alarm can be quickly identified.
Deciding which fire station will respond
Choosing the color of the alarm panel
Deciding how many people can live in the building
questions.n: Zoning allows responders to see exactly which part of a building (e.g., 'Floor 3, West Wing') has triggered an alarm.

questions.q: What is the standard wire color often used for fire alarm systems to distinguish them from general power wiring?
questions.n: Red is the universal color for fire protection systems, including wiring and conduits, for easy identification.

questions.q: Why are "End-of-Line" (EOL) resistors used in FDAS circuits?
o: To make the alarm sound louder
To monitor the integrity of the circuit and detect if a wire has been cut or damaged.
questions.n: The panel expects to see the resistance of the EOL; if the wire breaks, the resistance disappears, triggering a 'trouble' signal.

questions.q: When calculating Air Change Rates, what is the primary factor used besides the volume of the room?
o: The occupancy load and the nature of the activity in the room.
The price of the air conditioning unit
questions.n: The more people and the more intense the activity (e.g., cooking or exercise), the more fresh air is needed.

questions.q: Which HVAC component is responsible for moving air throughout the ductwork to achieve the required air change rate?
questions.n: The AHU contains the fan (blower) that pushes conditioned air into the ducts and through the building.

questions.q: In a plumbing diagram, what is the purpose of a "Check Valve"?
o: To filter out sand and dirt
To allow fluid to flow in only one direction and prevent backflow.
To increase the speed of the water
questions.n: It acts as a one-way gate, crucial for preventing contaminated water from flowing back into the clean supply.

questions.q: What is the difference between a "Direct" and "Indirect" waste pipe?
o: Direct pipes are made of plastic, indirect are made of metal
Direct pipes go to the sewer, indirect pipes go to the garden
An indirect waste pipe does not connect directly to the drainage system but discharges through an air gap or air break.
questions.n: Indirect waste is required for appliances like refrigerators or medical equipment to prevent sewage from backing up into them.

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of using a "Composite Slab" (metal deck + concrete) over a traditional RC slab?
o: It is cheaper to buy the metal than the wood for forms
Faster construction and the metal deck acts as both formwork and tensile reinforcement.
It makes the building much heavier
It is completely waterproof without any coating
questions.n: It eliminates the need for temporary plywood forms and reduces the amount of rebar needed at the bottom.

questions.q: For high-end residential plumbing, which brand of water closets is often specified for its "Siphon Jet" flushing technology?
o: Kohler or American Standard (Brands often cited in PH practice).
questions.n: These are the dominant high-spec brands in the Philippine market frequently seen in technical specifications.

questions.q: What is "Epoxy Injection" used for in site-based structural repair?
o: To fill and seal structural cracks in concrete to restore its integrity.
To kill termites inside the wall
questions.n: The low-viscosity epoxy is pumped into cracks under pressure to bond the concrete back together.

questions.q: In steel construction, what is the purpose of a "Base Plate"?
o: To decorate the bottom of the column
To distribute the concentrated load from a steel column to a larger area of the concrete foundation.
To prevent the column from getting wet
questions.n: Since steel is much stronger than concrete, the plate spreads the load so the column doesn't 'punch' through the pedestal.

questions.q: What is the common diameter of a "Sag Rod" used for light-gauge purlins?
questions.n: These are the standard sizes for sag rods in typical Philippine roof framing.

questions.q: Which material is most recommended for "Firestopping" penetrations in a floor slab (e.g., where pipes pass through)?
o: Fire-rated mineral wool or intumescent sealant.
questions.n: These materials expand when heated or resist melting to block fire and smoke from moving between floors.

questions.q: Why are "Temperature Bars" (Shrinkage reinforcement) placed in a concrete slab?
o: To increase the weight of the floor
To make the floor easier to polish
To prevent cracking caused by thermal expansion/contraction and drying shrinkage.
To keep the floor warm during the rainy season
questions.n: Concrete shrinks as it cures and expands/contracts with heat; these bars hold the concrete together against these forces.

questions.q: In a site layout, what is the purpose of the "Batter Boards"?
o: To serve as a fence for the construction site
To protect the workers from the sun
Horizontal boards nailed to stakes to hold the strings that mark the excavation and wall lines.
questions.n: They allow for the exact corners and wall positions to be relocated after digging starts.
